intro_html: Smoky chipotle, tomatoes, and lean pork come together in this Mexican-inspired tinga that costs almost nothing per bowl. The slow cooker does all the work while the flavor builds, then it all goes over rice. At around $2.45 a serving (at everyday cost) with 52 grams of protein, this one is hard to beat, and it makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $2.45 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each bowl comes in at 52 grams of protein and 569 calories across all 14 servings.
upsell_html: Big smoky flavor for pocket change is exactly the kind of win we like around here. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: One can of chipotle in adobo seasons the whole batch. A single small can does the job, so you do not need to buy much.
Store-brand diced tomatoes taste the same in a sauce as the name brands. Reach for the cheapest canned tomatoes every time.
Pork loin keeps this cheap and lean. Buy the loin over pre-shredded pork and do the shredding yourself in the pot.
make_it: Add the pork loin, sliced onions, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and stir in the chopped chipotle in adobo.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork shreds with a fork.
Shred the pork right in the pot and stir it back into the smoky sauce.
Cook the rice while the pork soaks up the flavor.
Spoon the saucy pork over the rice and serve.
